sentences.text:
13.09.2024 Order No.
08. 1. Heard.

2. At the instance of opposite party No.3, the F.I.R. dated 10.01.2021 in Banpur P.S. Case No.12 of 2021 for the offences under Sections 376(1)/323/294/506/34 of I.P.C. came to be registered against the petitioner.
During investigation, the parties have settled their dispute.

3. The opposite party No.3 being the complainant lodged an F.I.R. alleging therein that on 10.01.2021, his daughter being the opposite party No.2/victim was sexually assaulted by the petitioner, as a result of which, she became pregnant.
On 16.12.2020, she gave birth to a female child at Berhampur medical and the petitioner had co
-operated them in all respect.

After discharge from the medical, when the informant tried to send his daughter to the house of the petitioner, the petitioner and his family members offered some money to them and told that not to proceed with the case.
It is alleged that while they denied their proposal, the accused persons assaulted him and threatened to kill him and to his family members.
On the basis of such allegation, the F.I.R. was registered.
4. The petitioner and the opposite party Nos.2 & 3 are present in the Court and being represented and identified by their respective counsels.
They have also filed self-attested copies of their Aadhaar Cards to establish their identity, which are taken on record.

5. The petitioner and the opposite party Nos.2 & 3 have filed an affidavit dated 31.07.2024 inter alia stating as under:-

sentences.text: < 7 . That, as per terms and condition of settlement the petitioner will pay a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- (Five Lakhs) to the victim Opp-Party No.2 Manisha Begum towards her permanent alimony, and Similarly the petitioner will also make fix deposit of Rs.3,00,000/- (Three Lakhs) in the name of minor daughter Arifa Begum, to which both the victim/Opp-Party No.2 and informant agreed.
8. That, accordingly on 08.06.2024 the petitioner, deposited an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- (Three Lakhs) in the name of minor daughter Arifa Begum Banapur Post Office Account No-020118309252.
Similarly the petitioner has paid an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- (Five Lakhs) to the Opp-Party No-2 Manisha Begum towards her permanent alimony, when both the Opp-Party No-2 & 3 acknowledge the same.

9. That, in view of the above amicable settlement the victim as well as the informant the Opp-Party No-2 7 3 do not want to proceed further with in this case in the court of law as against the petitioner.=
6.
Mr. Mishra, learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State submits that he has received instruction from the I.I.C., Banpur P.S. on 06.08.2024.
In the said instruction, the I.I.C., Banpur P.S. has stated that the parties have indeed settled their dispute and the victim has been appropriately compensated.

Mr. Mishra, further submits that since the parties have settled their dispute, therefore, there is no legal impediment in quashing the F.I.R.
7.

Regard being had to the fact that the parties have settled their dispute and keeping in view the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and another reported in 2012 (10) SCC 303 and B.S. Joshi & others vs. State of Haryana & another reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675, I am of the considered view that subjecting the petitioner to trial would be a futile exercise.

sentences.text: Therefore, the petition deserves merit.

8. Accordingly, the criminal proceeding in connection with G.R. Case No.15 of 2021 arising out of Banpur P.S. Case No.12 of 2021 pending in the Court of the learned J.M.F.C., Banpur and the consequential proceedings arising therefrom qua the petitioner are quashed.
9. The CRLMC is accordingly disposed of.
(S.S. Mishra) Judge Swarna Location: High Court of Orissa Rahaman Khan vs State Of Odisha And Others ....
